|url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''|四隅突出形|}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan. They are associated with the [[Asuka Period]], [[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] in [[Fuchū, Tokyo|Fuchū]] in Tokyo, and [[Miyazuka Kofun]] are two notable examples. ==== List of Joenkahofun ==== * {{ill|Ishino Karato Kofun|ja|石のカラト古墳}} * {{ill|Sanno-zuka Ancient Tomb|ja|山王塚古墳}} * {{ill|Shimizu Yanagikita No. 1 Tomb|ja|清水柳北1号墳}} * {{ill|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun|ja|天文台構内古墳|1=Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} * {{ill|Nochi Kubo Ancient Tomb|ja|野地久保古墳}} * [[Miyazuka Kofun]] * [[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] {{clear}} === Corridor-type kofun === [[File:Yoshimi Yoshimi-hyakuana from afar.jpg|thumb|[[Yoshimi Hundred Caves]] a group of Corridor-type Kofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|corridor-type kofun|lt=cave tomb|kk=-type kofun|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb}}|横穴墓|Yokōbo}} are a kind of Kofun dug as artificial caves in [[Ancient Japan]].{{Cite web |title=Sakushima Ancient Tomb Mounds (Kofun) – 西尾観光 |url=https://nishiokanko.com/en/nishio-sakushima-island/kofun/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=nishiokanko.com}}{{Cite web |title=Unique burial concepts: Diversity of tomb systems｜Southern Kyushu's Remarkable Kofun Culture｜Kofun as World Cultural Heritage [[File:NintokuTomb_Aerial_photograph_2007.jpg|thumb|The [[Zenpokoenfun]] where [[Emperor Nintoku]] is buried in [[Mozu tombs]]]] '''Zenpokoenfun''' are a notable type of Japanese ancient tombs (Kofun), which consists of a square front part ({{Lang|ja|前方部}}) and a circular back part ({{Lang|ja|後円部}}).{{Kotobank|display=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} The part connecting the two is called the middlepart ({{Lang|ja|くびれ部}}), which looks like a [[Lock and key|keyhole]] when viewed from above.{{Cite web |date=2019-10-03 |title=What are these keyhole-shaped mounds? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-asia-49757034 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116105058/https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-asia-49757034 |archive-date=2020-11-16 {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisen Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[Mozu kofungun]], [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai]], [[Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[Haniwa]], [[terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisen Kofun]] in [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisen Kofun]] of the [[Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. ([[Danpusan Kofun]] ([[Nagoya]]), 6th century) ===Late Kofun period=== Keyhole-shaped kofun disappeared in the late 6th century AD, probably due to the drastic reformation in the Yamato court, where {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} records the introduction of [[Buddhism]] during this era. ==Types== === {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} === [[File:Gyoda_Maruhakayama_Kofun_In_Spring_1.JPG|thumb|A round Kofun]] {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} are a kind of Kofun{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} {{Clear}} === Square Kofun === [[File:Otozuka Kofun Door.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Otozuka Kofun|ja|乙塚古墳|12=draft}}, A Square Kofun]] {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (方墳, hōfun) is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} They are not as common as [[Zenpokoenfun]] of Keyhole shaped Kofun.{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2022-10-24 |title=iCLA Students Study Ancient Kofun with Dr. Darren Ashmore |url=https://www.icla.ygu.ac.jp/en/icla-students-study-ancient-burial-mound-with-dr-darren-ashmore/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=International College of Liberal Arts (iCLA) |language=en-US}}{{clear}} === Scallop Kofun === [[File:CG_Otomeyama_Kofun_2_7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of Kofun. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}}{{Cite book |last=Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf |title=Chapter 2: Description |pages=21–163 |chapter=}} Famous examples include [[Hokenoyama Kofun]] in the [[Makimuku ruins]].{{Cite web |title=Hokenoyama Kofun - Long Barrow in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=53966 |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=The Megalithic Portal}}{{Citation |last=Kidder |first=J. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''|四隅突出形|}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|12=draft}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisen Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[Mozu kofungun]], [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai]], [[Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[Haniwa]], [[terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisen Kofun]] in [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisen Kofun]] of the [[Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. File:CG Gosashi Kofun 1 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Early Kofun period''' which was drawn in [[3DCG]].
([[Gosashi tomb|Gosashi Kofun]] ([[Nara, Nara]]), 4th century) File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
({{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|12=draft}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) File:CG Danpusan Kofun 6 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Late Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
([[Danpusan Kofun]] ([[Nagoya]]), 6th century) ===Late Kofun period=== Keyhole-shaped kofun disappeared in the late 6th century AD, probably due to the drastic reformation in the Yamato court, where {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} records the introduction of [[Buddhism]] during this era. ==Types== === {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} === [[File:Gyoda_Maruhakayama_Kofun_In_Spring_1.JPG|thumb|A round Kofun]] {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} are a kind of Kofun{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} {{Clear}} === Square Kofun === [[File:Otozuka Kofun Door.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Otozuka Kofun|ja|乙塚古墳|12=draft}}, A Square Kofun]] {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} (方墳, hōfun) is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} They are not as common as [[Zenpokoenfun]] of Keyhole shaped Kofun.{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2022-10-24 |title=iCLA Students Study Ancient Kofun with Dr. Darren Ashmore |url=https://www.icla.ygu.ac.jp/en/icla-students-study-ancient-burial-mound-with-dr-darren-ashmore/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=International College of Liberal Arts (iCLA) |language=en-US}}{{clear}} === Scallop Kofun === [[File:CG_Otomeyama_Kofun_2_7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of Kofun. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}}{{Cite book |last=Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf |title=Chapter 2: Description |pages=21–163 |chapter=}} Famous examples include [[Hokenoyama Kofun]] in the [[Makimuku ruins]].{{Cite web |title=Hokenoyama Kofun - Long Barrow in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=53966 |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=The Megalithic Portal}}{{Citation |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780824862848/html |work=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai |access-date=2023-11-10 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |language=en |doi=10.1515/9780824862848 |isbn=978-0-8248-6284-8}}{{rp|249}} dated to around 250 AD.{{rp|253}} and [[Nyotaizan Kofun]]. {{clear}} === Octagonal Kofun === [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|[[Kengoshizuka Kofun]] a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of Kofun. They are a very rare kind characteristic of Emperors Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in [[Kengoshizuka Kofun]]., [[Emperor Tenji]] in [[Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|his Mausoleum]],{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}} and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}} From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==== List of Octagonal Kofun ==== * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|12=draft}} * {{ill|Inari Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|12=draft}}* [[Kajiyama Kofun]] * [[Kengoshizuka Kofun]] * {{ill|Gobyo Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft}} * [[Takei temple ruins]] * {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|12=draft}} * [[Nakayamasōen Kofun]] * {{ill|King Noguchi Kofun|ja|野口王墓|12=draft}} * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=draft}} * [[Yoshida Kofun]] {{clear}} === Zenpō-kōhō-fun === [[File:大安場古墳1号墳.JPG|thumb|[[Ōyasuba Kofun group|Ōyasuba Kofun]] a Zenpō-kōhō-fun]] [[File:Kofun06.jpg|thumb|general diagram of a zenpō-kōhō-fun]] {{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}''|前方後方墳|4=two conjoined rectangles kofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}}{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |language=en}} They are shaped somewhat like the more keyhole shaped [[Zenpokoenfun]], but they have a square body rather than a circular one.{{Cite book |last1=Laporte |first1=Luc |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HO6CEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA722 |title=Megaliths of the World |last2=Large |first2=Jean-Marc |last3=Nespoulous |first3=Laurent |last4=Scarre |first4=Chris |last5=Steimer-Herbet |first5=Tara |date=2022-08-22 |publisher=Archaeopress Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-1-80327-321-1 |pages=722 |language=en}} They tend to be smaller than [[Zenpokoenfun]].{{Cite book |last1=Ikehara-Tsukayama |first1=Hugo C. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gBNgEAAAQBAJ&dq=Zenp%C5%8D-k%C5%8Dh%C5%8D-fun&pg=PA103 |title=Global Perspectives on Landscapes of Warfare |last2=Ruiz |first2=Juan Carlos Vargas |date=2022-04-18 |publisher=University Press of Colorado |isbn=978-1-64642-211-1 |language=en}} [[Yanaida Nunōyama Kofun]] is one of the largest of the type{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''|四隅突出形|}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|12=draft}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan. They are associated with the [[Asuka Period]], [[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] in [[Fuchū, Tokyo|Fuchū]] in Tokyo, and [[Miyazuka Kofun]] are two notable examples. ==== List of Joenkahofun ==== * {{ill|Ishino Karato Kofun|ja|石のカラト古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Sanno-zuka Ancient Tomb|ja|山王塚古墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Shimizu Yanagikita No. 1 Tomb|ja|清水柳北1号墳|12=draft}} * {{ill|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun|ja|天文台構内古墳|1=Tenmondai Kounai Kofun|12=draft}} * {{ill|Nochi Kubo Ancient Tomb|ja|野地久保古墳|12=draft}} * [[Miyazuka Kofun]] * [[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] {{clear}} === Corridor-type kofun === [[File:Yoshimi Yoshimi-hyakuana from afar.jpg|thumb|[[Yoshimi Hundred Caves]] a group of Corridor-type Kofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|corridor-type kofun|lt=cave tomb|kk=-type kofun|ja|横穴墓|1=Cave tomb|12=draft}}|横穴墓|Yokōbo}} are a kind of Kofun dug as artificial caves in [[Ancient Japan]].{{Cite web |title=Sakushima Ancient Tomb Mounds (Kofun) – 西尾観光 |url=https://nishiokanko.com/en/nishio-sakushima-island/kofun/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=nishiokanko.com}}{{Cite web |title=Unique burial concepts: Diversity of tomb systems｜Southern Kyushu's Remarkable Kofun Culture｜Kofun as World Cultural Heritage |url=https://www.miyazaki-archive.jp/d-museum/mk-heritage/en/specialmention/urial_thought.html |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=www.miyazaki-archive.jp}}https://www.rekihaku.ac.jp/english/outline/publication/ronbun/ronbun9/pdf/217011.pdf{{clear}} === Zenpokoenfun === {{Main|Zenpokoenfun}} [[File:NintokuTomb_Aerial_photograph_2007.jpg|thumb|The [[Zenpokoenfun]] where [[Emperor Nintoku]] is buried in [[Mozu tombs]]]] '''Zenpokoenfun''' are a notable type of Japanese ancient tombs (Kofun), which consists of a square front part ({{Lang|ja|前方部}}) and a circular back part ({{Lang|ja|後円部}}).{{Kotobank|display=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} The part connecting the two is called the middlepart ({{Lang|ja|くびれ部}}), which looks like a [[Lock and key|keyhole]] when viewed from above.{{Cite web |date=2019-10-03 |title=What are these keyhole-shaped mounds? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-asia-49757034 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116105058/https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-asia-49757034 |archive-date=2020-11-16 {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisen Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[Mozu kofungun]], [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai]], [[Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[Haniwa]], [[terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisen Kofun]] in [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisen Kofun]] of the [[Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. ([[Danpusan Kofun]] ([[Nagoya]]), 6th century) ===Late Kofun period=== Keyhole-shaped kofun disappeared in the late 6th century AD, probably due to the drastic reformation in the Yamato court, where {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} records the introduction of [[Buddhism]] during this era. ==Types== === {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft}} === [[File:Gyoda_Maruhakayama_Kofun_In_Spring_1.JPG|thumb|A round Kofun]] {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft}} are a kind of Kofun{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} {{Clear}} === Square Kofun === [[File:Otozuka Kofun Door.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Otozuka Kofun|ja|乙塚古墳|qq=draft}}, A Square Kofun]] {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft}} (方墳, hōfun) is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} They are not as common as [[Zenpokoenfun]] of Keyhole shaped Kofun.{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2022-10-24 |title=iCLA Students Study Ancient Kofun with Dr. Darren Ashmore |url=https://www.icla.ygu.ac.jp/en/icla-students-study-ancient-burial-mound-with-dr-darren-ashmore/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=International College of Liberal Arts (iCLA) |language=en-US}}{{clear}} === Scallop Kofun === [[File:CG_Otomeyama_Kofun_2_7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft}} is a kind of Kofun. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft}}{{Cite book |last=Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf |title=Chapter 2: Description |pages=21–163 |chapter=}} Famous examples include [[Hokenoyama Kofun]] in the [[Makimuku ruins]].{{Cite web |title=Hokenoyama Kofun - Long Barrow in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=53966 |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=The Megalithic Portal}}{{Citation |last=Kidder |first=J. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''|四隅突出形|}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan. {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisen Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[Mozu kofungun]], [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai]], [[Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/empun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hōfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[Haniwa]], [[terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisen Kofun]] in [[Sakai, Osaka|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisen Kofun]] of the [[Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. File:CG Gosashi Kofun 1 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Early Kofun period''' which was drawn in [[3DCG]].
([[Gosashi tomb|Gosashi Kofun]] ([[Nara, Nara]]), 4th century) File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
({{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuyama Kofun|qq=}} ([[Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) File:CG Danpusan Kofun 6 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Late Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
([[Danpusan Kofun]] ([[Nagoya]]), 6th century) ===Late Kofun period=== Keyhole-shaped kofun disappeared in the late 6th century AD, probably due to the drastic reformation in the Yamato court, where {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} records the introduction of [[Buddhism]] during this era. ==Types== === {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} === [[File:Gyoda_Maruhakayama_Kofun_In_Spring_1.JPG|thumb|A round Kofun]] {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}} are a kind of Kofun{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} {{Clear}} === Square Kofun === [[File:Otozuka Kofun Door.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Otozuka Kofun|ja|乙塚古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otozuka Kofun|qq=}}, A Square Kofun]] {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} (方墳, hōfun) is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} They are not as common as [[Zenpokoenfun]] of Keyhole shaped Kofun.{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2022-10-24 |title=iCLA Students Study Ancient Kofun with Dr. Darren Ashmore |url=https://www.icla.ygu.ac.jp/en/icla-students-study-ancient-burial-mound-with-dr-darren-ashmore/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=International College of Liberal Arts (iCLA) |language=en-US}}{{clear}} === Scallop Kofun === [[File:CG_Otomeyama_Kofun_2_7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}} is a kind of Kofun. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=}}{{Cite book |last=Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf |title=Chapter 2: Description |pages=21–163 |chapter=}} Famous examples include [[Hokenoyama Kofun]] in the [[Makimuku ruins]].{{Cite web |title=Hokenoyama Kofun - Long Barrow in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=53966 |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=The Megalithic Portal}}{{Citation |last=Kidder |first=J. lang|ja}}. There is a specific style exemplified by [[Yadani Kofun]] and [[Jinyama Kofun Cluster]] and '''Rokuji Kozuka Kofun''' and '''Tomisaki Kofungun''' of [[Ōzuka-Senbōyama Sites]] as {{nihongo|''yosumi-tosshutsugata''|四隅突出形|}}, which is square or rectangular, with protrusions on each of its four corners; however, it is unique in that it is not a true rectangle, but has a narrow waist, similar to a "two conjoined rectangles" type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=}}''|前方後方墳|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}). The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan.
