{{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisenryō Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu kofungun]], [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[:en:Northeast Asia|Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[:en:Zempō-kōen fun|Zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[:en:Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[:en:World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/empun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hōfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]], [[terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisenryō Kofun]] in [[:en:Sakai|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[:en:Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[:en:en:List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[:en:Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[:en:Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[:en:Kurashiki, Okayama|Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[:en:San'in region|San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[:en:Bronze mirrors|Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[:en:Yamataikoku|Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[:en:Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisenryō Kofun]] of the [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. File:CG Gosashi Kofun 1 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Early Kofun period''' which was drawn in [[:en:3DCG|3DCG]].
([[Gosashi Kofun|Gosashi Kofun]] ([[:en:Nara (city)|Nara (city)]]), 4th century) File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
({{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuyama Kofun|qq=}} ([[:en:Fujiidera, Osaka|Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) File:CG Danpusan Kofun 6 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Late Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
([[Danpusan Kofun]] ([[:en:Nagoya|Nagoya]]), 6th century) ===Late Kofun period=== Keyhole-shaped kofun disappeared in the late 6th century AD, probably due to the drastic reformation in the Yamato court, where {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} records the introduction of [[:en:Buddhism|Buddhism]] during this era. ==Types== === {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} === [[File:Gyoda_Maruhakayama_Kofun_In_Spring_1.JPG|thumb|A round Kofun]] {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} are a kind of Kofun{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} {{Clear}} === Square Kofun === [[File:Otozuka Kofun Door.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Otozuka Kofun|ja|乙塚古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otozuka Kofun|qq=}}, A Square Kofun]] {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (方墳, hōfun) is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=About kofun -Scale and order- {{!}} Nonaka Kofun-Project for the Preservation and Utilization of Artifacts from Nonaka Kofun/Osaka University Department of Archaeology |url=https://www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp/kouko/nonaka/en/ancient_tomb_period/ancient_tomb_period01.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.let.osaka-u.ac.jp}} They are not as common as [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] of Keyhole shaped Kofun.{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2022-10-24 |title=iCLA Students Study Ancient Kofun with Dr. Darren Ashmore |url=https://www.icla.ygu.ac.jp/en/icla-students-study-ancient-burial-mound-with-dr-darren-ashmore/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=International College of Liberal Arts (iCLA) |language=en-US}}{{clear}} === Scallop Kofun === [[File:CG_Otomeyama_Kofun_2_7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} is a kind of Kofun. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisenryō Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu kofungun]], [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[:en:Northeast Asia|Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[:en:Zempō-kōen fun|Zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[:en:Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[:en:World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/empun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hōfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]], [[terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisenryō Kofun]] in [[:en:Sakai|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[:en:Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[:en:en:List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[:en:Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[:en:Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[:en:Kurashiki, Okayama|Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[:en:San'in region|San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[:en:Bronze mirrors|Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[:en:Yamataikoku|Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[:en:Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisenryō Kofun]] of the [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. type of Japanese ancient tombs (Kofun), which consists of a square front part ({{Lang|ja|前方部}}) and a circular back part ({{Lang|ja|後円部}}).{{Kotobank|display=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} The part connecting the two is called the middlepart ({{Lang|ja|くびれ部}}), which looks like a [[Lock and key|keyhole]] when viewed from above.{{Cite web |date=2019-10-03 |title=What are these keyhole-shaped mounds? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-asia-49757034 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116105058/https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-asia-49757034 |archive-date=2020-11-16 {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisenryō Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu kofungun]], [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[:en:Northeast Asia|Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[:en:Zempō-kōen fun|Zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[:en:Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[:en:World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/empun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hōfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]], [[:en:Terracotta|Terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisenryō Kofun]] in [[:en:Sakai|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[:en:Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[:en:en:List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[:en:Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[:en:Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[:en:Kurashiki, Okayama|Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[:en:San'in region|San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[:en:Bronze mirrors|Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[:en:Yamataikoku|Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[:en:Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisenryō Kofun]] of the [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan. They are associated with the [[:en:Asuka Period|Asuka Period]], [[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] in [[:en:Fuchū, Tokyo|Fuchū]] in Tokyo, and [[Miyazuka Kofun]] are two notable examples. ==== List [[File:NintokuTomb_Aerial_photograph_2007.jpg|thumb|The [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] where [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] is buried in [[Mozu tombs]]]] '''Zenpokoenfun''' are a notable type of Japanese ancient tombs (Kofun), which consists of a square front part ({{Lang|ja|前方部}}) and a circular back part ({{Lang|ja|後円部}}).{{Kotobank|display=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} The part connecting the two is called the middlepart ({{Lang|ja|くびれ部}}), which looks like a [[Lock and key|keyhole]] when viewed from above.{{Cite web |date=2019-10-03 |title=What are these keyhole-shaped mounds? {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisenryō Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu kofungun]], [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[:en:Tomb|Tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[:en:Northeast Asia|Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[:en:Zempō-kōen fun|Zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[:en:Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[:en:World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]], [[:en:Terracotta|Terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisenryō Kofun]] in [[:en:Sakai|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[:en:Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[:en:en:List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[:en:Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[:en:Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[:en:Kurashiki, Okayama|Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[:en:San'in region|San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[:en:Bronze mirrors|Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[:en:Yamataikoku|Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[:en:Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisenryō Kofun]] of the [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan. {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisenryō Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu kofungun]], [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[:en:Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[:en:Tomb|Tomb]]s or [[tumulus|tumuli]] in [[:en:Northeast Asia|Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[:en:Zempō-kōen fun|Zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[:en:Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[:en:World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/empun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}), and square-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|hōfun|lt=hōfun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/hōfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}}) kofun. Orientation of kofun is not specified. For example, in the Saki ''kofun'' group, all of the circular parts are facing north, but there is no such formation in the Yanagimoto ''kofun'' group. [[:en:Haniwa|Haniwa]], [[:en:Terracotta|Terracotta]] figures, were arrayed above and in the surroundings to delimit and protect the sacred areas. ''Kofun'' range from several metres to over 400 m long. The largest, which has been attributed to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], is [[Daisenryō Kofun]] in [[:en:Sakai|Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture]]. The funeral chamber was located beneath the round part and comprised a group of megaliths. In 1972, the unlooted [[Takamatsuzuka Tomb]] was found in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka]], and some details of the discovery were revealed. Inside the tightly assembled rocks, white [[:en:Lime (mineral)|lime]] plasters were pasted, and colored pictures depict the 'Asuka Beauties' of the court as well as constellations. A stone coffin was placed in the chamber, and accessories, swords, and bronze mirrors were laid both inside and outside the coffin. The wall paintings have been designated [[:en:en:List of National Treasures of Japan (paintings)|national treasures]] and the grave goods as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|important cultural property]], while the tumulus is a [[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|special historic site]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2020 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9951 |title=Database of National Cultural Properties |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 May 2011}} ===Locations and number=== ''Kofun'' Kofuns and their remains have been found all over Japan, including remote islands such as [[:en:Nishinoshima (Shimane)|Nishinoshima]].[http://iseki.ipc.shimane-u.ac.jp/search.php?&search_kbn=city&sitecitycode%5B%5D=58&target=site&order_item=siteshimpsiteno 島根県遺跡データベース　Archaeological Database of Shimane（Japanese）] A total of 161,560 kofun tomb sites have been found as of 2001. [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] has the most of all prefectures (16,577 sites), and [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] has the second most (13,112 sites).[http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/kihonkousou/6(4).pdf 兵庫県教育委員会 兵庫県の遺跡・遺物数の全国的な位置（pdf file, Japanese）] == History == [[File:IshibutaiWithFigureSmallVersion2.jpg|thumb|The stone chamber of [[Ishibutai Kofun]], said to be the tomb of [[Soga no Umako]], [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]] (7th century)]] [[File:Seta_Iseki_(Kashihara),_shuko-bo.JPG|thumb|Circular groove tomb at Seta Ruins (Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture)]] ===Yayoi period=== Most of the tombs of chiefs in the [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi period]] were square-shaped mounds surrounded by ditches. The most notable example in the late Yayoi period is [[:en:Tatetsuki Site|Tatetsuki Mound Tomb]] in [[:en:Kurashiki, Okayama|Kurashiki, Okayama]]. The mound is about 45 metres wide and 5 metres high and has a shaft chamber. Broken pieces of ''Tokushu-kidai'', cylindrical earthenware, were excavated around the mound. Another prevalent type of Yayoi period tomb is the ''Yosumi tosshutsugata funkyūbo'', a square mound with protruding corners. These tombs were built in the [[:en:San'in region|San'in region]], a coastal area off the Sea of Japan. Unearthed articles indicate the existence of alliances between native tribes in the region. ===Early Kofun period=== [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|Panoramic view of Hashinaka Kofun in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]]]] One of the first keyhole-shaped kofun was built in the {{interlanguage link|Makimuku ruins|lt=Makimuku|ja|纒向型前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} area,{{Cite web|url=http://sitereports.nabunken.go.jp/1654|title=たわらもと2013発掘速報展|last=Krako-kagi Archaeological Museum|date=2013|website=Comprehensive Database of Archaeological Site Reports in Japan|access-date=2016-09-01}} the southeastern part of the Nara Basin. [[:en:Hashihaka Kofun|Hashihaka Kofun]], which was built in the middleof the 3rd century AD, is 280 metres long and 30 metres high. Its scale is obviously different from previous Yayoi tombs. During the next three decades, about 10 kofun were built in the area, which are now called as the ''Makimuku Kofun Group''. A wooden coffin was placed on the bottom of a shaft, and the surrounding walls were built up by flat stones. Finally, megalithic stones formed the roof. [[:en:Bronze mirrors|Bronze mirrors]], iron swords, ''[[magatama]]'', clay vessels and other artifacts were found in good condition in undisturbed tombs. Some scholars assume the buried person of ''Hashihaka kofun'' was the shadowy ancient Queen [[Himiko]] of [[:en:Yamataikoku|Yamataikoku]], mentioned in the Chinese historical texts. According to the books, Japan was called [[:en:Wa (Japan)|Wa]], which was the confederation of numerous small tribes or countries. The construction of gigantic kofun is the result of the relatively centralized governmental structure in the Nara Basin, possibly the origin of the Yamato polity and the Imperial lineage of Japan. ===Mid-Kofun period=== During the 5th century AD, the construction of keyhole kofun began in [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]; continued in Kawachi, where gigantic kofun, such as [[Daisenryō Kofun]] of the [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]], were built; and then throughout the country. The proliferation of keyhole kofun is generally assumed to be evidence of the Yamato court's expansion in this age. However, some argue that it simply shows the spread of culture based on progress in distribution, and has little to do with a political breakthrough. A few tombs from the mid-Baekje era were excavated around the Yeongsan River basin in South Korea.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} The design of these tombs are notably different. The tombs that were discovered on the Korean peninsula were built between the 5th and 6th centuries CE.{{Citation needed|date=January 2021}} There remain questions about who were buried in these tombs such as nobility, aristocracy, warriors or mercenaries. File:CG Gosashi Kofun 1 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Early Kofun period''' which was drawn in [[:en:3DCG|3DCG]].
([[Gosashi Kofun|Gosashi Kofun]] ([[:en:Nara (city)|Nara (city)]]), 4th century) File:CG Nakatsuyama kofun Southeast.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Mid-Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
({{ill|Nakatsuyama Kofun|ja|仲ツ山古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakatsuyama Kofun|qq=}} ([[:en:Fujiidera, Osaka|Fujiidera, Osaka]]), 5th century) File:CG Danpusan Kofun 6 7p.jpg|An example of keyhole-shaped mound in the '''Late Kofun period''' which was drawn in 3DCG.
([[Danpusan Kofun]] ([[:en:Nagoya|Nagoya]]), 6th century) ===Late Kofun period=== Keyhole-shaped kofun disappeared in the late 6th century AD, probably due to the drastic reformation in the Yamato court, where {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} records the introduction of [[:en:Buddhism|Buddhism]] during this era. ==Types== === {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} === [[File:Gyoda_Maruhakayama_Kofun_In_Spring_1.JPG|thumb|A round Kofun]] |url=https://www.icla.ygu.ac.jp/en/icla-students-study-ancient-burial-mound-with-dr-darren-ashmore/ |access-date=2023-10-23 |website=International College of Liberal Arts (iCLA) |language=en-US}}{{clear}} === Scallop Kofun === [[File:CG_Otomeyama_Kofun_2_7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} is a kind of Kofun. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}{{Cite book |last=Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group |url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/sekai_isan/ichiran/pdf/r1419077_06.pdf |title=Chapter 2: Description |pages=21–163 |chapter=}} Famous examples include [[Hokenoyama Kofun]] in the [[Makimuku ruins]].{{Cite web |title=Hokenoyama Kofun - Long Barrow in Japan in Honshū |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=53966 |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=The Megalithic Portal}}{{Citation |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780824862848/html |work=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai |access-date=2023-11-10 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |language=en |doi=10.1515/9780824862848 |isbn=978-0-8248-6284-8}}{{rp|249}} dated to around 250 AD.{{rp|253}} and [[Nyotaizan Kofun]]. {{clear}} === Octagonal Kofun === [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|[[Kengoshizuka Kofun]] a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of Kofun. They are a very rare kind characteristic of Emperors Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]] in [[Kengoshizuka Kofun]]., [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] in [[Gobyō-no-Kofun|his Mausoleum]],{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21}} and [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]] |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal |archive-date=2023-10-16 |access-date=2023-10-20}} From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' The slope of the mound is covered with ''[[fukiishi]]'' -like stones, with a row of larger stones marking its edge, and is surrounded by a two-meter wide moat. The ''yosumi-tosshutsugata'' style is unique to the late middleYayoi period and is most prevalent in western Japan in areas influenced by the [[:en:Izumo Province|Izumo culture]].{{clear}} === Joenkahofun === [[File:Musashi-Fuchu_Kumano-jinja_Kofun,_funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|[[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] a Joenkahofun]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Joenkahofun|lt=Joenkahofun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}} is a kind of Kofun.{{Cite web |title=Nara National Research Institute for Cultural Properties |url=https://www.nabunken.go.jp/english/monograph/72.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.nabunken.go.jp}}{{Cite web |title=Kofun Culture |url=http://www.t-net.ne.jp/~keally/kofun.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=www.t-net.ne.jp}}{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}} Such kofun have a round dome top with a square bottom. This is a quite rare type of Kofun in Japan. They are associated with the [[:en:Asuka Period|Asuka Period]], [[Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] in [[:en:Fuchū, Tokyo|Fuchū]] in Tokyo, and [[Miyazuka Kofun]] are two notable examples. ==== List {{Short description|Megalithic tombs in Northeast Asia}} {{For|the period of Japanese history|Kofun period}} {{Italic title|reason=}} [[Image:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|[[Daisenryō Kofun]], the largest of all kofun, one of many tumuli in the [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu kofungun]], [[:en:Sakai|Sakai]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]] (5th century)]] {{Nihongo|'''''Kofun'''''|古墳|4=from [[:en:Sino-Japanese vocabulary|Sino-Japanese]] "ancient grave"}} are megalithic [[:en:Tomb|Tomb]]s or [[:en:Tumulus|tumuli]] in [[:en:Northeast Asia|Northeast Asia]]. ''Kofun'' were mainly constructed in the [[Japanese archipelago]] between the middleof the 3rd century to the early 7th century AD.岡田裕之「前方後円墳」『日本古代史大辞典』大和書房、2006th year 。{{ISBN|978-4479840657}} The term is the origin of the name of the [[Kofun period]], which indicates the middle3rd century to early–middle6th century. Many ''kofun'' have distinctive keyhole-shaped mounds ({{nihongo|3=[[:en:Zempō-kōen fun|Zempō-kōen fun]]|2=前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}). The [[:en:Mozu kofungun|Mozu]]-[[:en:Furuichi kofungun|Furuichi]] kofungun or tumulus clusters were inscribed on the [[:en:World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] in 2019, while [[Ishibutai Kofun]] is one of a number in [[:en:Asuka-Fujiwara|Asuka-Fujiwara]] residing on the [[World Heritage Sites in Japan#Tentative List|Tentative List]].{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5570/ |title=Mozu-Furuichi Kofungun, Ancient Kofun Clusters |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}}{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5097/ |title=Asuka-Fujiwara: Archaeological sites of Japan's Ancient Capitals and Related Properties |publisher=[[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] |access-date=18 May 2011}} == Overview == The ''kofun tumuli'' have assumed various shapes throughout history. The most common type of ''kofun'' is known as a {{nihongo|''[[:en:Zenpokoenfun|zenpō-kōen-fun]]''|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, which is shaped like a keyhole, having one square end and one circular end, when viewed from above. There are also circular-type ({{nihongo|''{{ill|empun|lt=empun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/empun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}}), "two conjoined rectangles" typed ({{ill|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because of the mass replacement error that gets rid of the links like this otherwise|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}''|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped
